title: Sorted Suspects
subtitle: The cricket league needs its scoreboard sorted
conceptSummary: ORDER BY sorts your results. Add DESC for highest-first, ASC (default) for lowest-first.

dialogue.text: The Cricket League commissioner wants to know who scored the most runs. The data is all jumbled!
Use ORDER BY. Sort by runs, highest to lowest. Simple.
Let's find the top scorers and see if anything in the stats looks... fixed.

teachMoment.title: Sorting Results with ORDER BY
teachMoment.body:
ORDER BY sorts your results:

SELECT name, runs_scored FROM match_stats ORDER BY runs_scored DESC

• DESC = Descending (highest first — 100, 90, 80...)
• ASC = Ascending (lowest first — 10, 20, 30...)
• Default is ASC if you don't specify

task.instruction: Find all match stats and sort by runs_scored from HIGHEST to LOWEST. Show player_id, match_id, and runs_scored.
task.startingQuery:
SELECT player_id, match_id, runs_scored
FROM match_stats
ORDER BY
task.solution: SELECT player_id, match_id, runs_scored FROM match_stats ORDER BY runs_scored DESC

hints.text: You need ORDER BY after the table name. What column should be sorted?
Highest to lowest = DESC. So: ORDER BY runs_scored DESC
Full: SELECT player_id, match_id, runs_scored FROM match_stats ORDER BY runs_scored DESC

winDialogue.text: Player 14 — Jake Williams — scored a suspiciously high 112 runs as a BOWLER. That's almost impossible!
Someone doctored those match stats. And if they're messing with cricket, they're messing with betting data too.

storyBeat: Match stats have been tampered with. A bowler with 112 runs. The trail leads to a shadowy data manipulation ring. SHADOW42 is more than a pizza discount code.
